# Liberal Democrats Manifesto 2019: Summary

## Stop Brexit, Build a Brighter Future

The Liberal Democrats position themselves as the only party offering a clear, forward-looking vision for Britain. Their fundamental message is unequivocal: stop Brexit and remain in the European Union. They argue that EU membership secures a £50 billion "Remain Bonus" through stronger economic growth, which would be invested in public services, schools, and tackling inequality.

## Core Values and Vision

The party champions building a fair, free, and open society balancing liberty, equality, and community. They reject what they characterise as the "tired old parties"—Conservatives pursuing "1870s" ideas and Labour offering "1970s" socialism—presenting themselves as the natural home for business and progressive voters alike.

## Economic Plan

Liberal Democrats propose £130 billion in infrastructure investment, including renewable energy, transport systems, broadband, and housing. Their innovation-led economy vision targets increasing R&D spending to 3% of GDP. They would introduce Skills Wallets—£10,000 per adult for lifelong learning—recognising that careers increasingly require continuous retraining.

## Climate Emergency

The party commits to achieving net-zero emissions by 2045 through an emergency ten-year programme: generating 80% of electricity from renewables by 2030, insulating homes to end fuel poverty by 2025, banning fracking, and planting 60 million trees annually.

## Public Services

They pledge a 1p Income Tax rise to raise £7 billion annually for NHS and social care, ring-fenced for mental health equality, workforce recruitment, and service improvements. Education priorities include reversing school cuts, hiring 20,000 additional teachers, and providing free childcare from nine months for working parents.

## Social Justice and Rights

The manifesto promises to fix the "broken" Universal Credit system, build 100,000 social homes annually, end rough sleeping within five years, and scrap the Conservatives' "hostile environment" immigration policies. They champion human rights, civil liberties, and equality—including completing gender recognition reform and extending voting rights.

## Political Reform

Advocating proportional representation, votes at 16, and a federal UK structure, they seek to transform British democracy, devolving power to nations, regions, and communities while maintaining strong international partnerships.
